items.title: Russia launches largest attack on Ukraine energy infrastructure since spring
items.description: In total 11 regions of the country were attacked overnight, with residential buildings and railways also targeted, the Ukrainian PM says.

items.title: Last UK and US troops leave Iraq as anti-Islamic State mission ends
items.description: The withdrawal of coalition forces, under a deal agreed two years ago, was a key demand of the Iraqi government.

items.title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons
items.description: Mindgard said it discovered in July that Kimi models K2.6 and K3 Swarm could evade developer's safety limits.

items.title: Girl has multiple surgeries to control infections after strike in Gaza
items.description: Witnesses say Raseel's tent was hit by an Israeli helicopter strike. Israel’s military says it has no record of the attack.

items.title: US actor Chad Lowe 'heartbroken' by death of daughter Fiona aged 13
items.description: Lowe and his wife Kim Painter announce the death of their daughter, who "was the light of our lives".

items.title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after more than 100 allege brain injuries
items.description: Hundreds of riders were allegedly injured on X2, which has seats that spin 360 degrees.

items.title: South Korea demands apology from Pyongyang for landmine blasts that injured three
items.description: Blasts in the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) injured three South Korean personnel earlier this month.

items.title: Botswana condemned for slaughtering elephants for independence celebrations
items.description: The government authorises the hunting of 23 elephants and dozens of other wild animals for independence day feasts.

items.title: US Supreme Court denies Christa Pike's last-ditch bid to halt execution
items.description: The Tennessee inmate has been awaiting execution since she was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of a teenage classmate.

items.title: Africa's richest man launches Kenya oil refinery despite land protests
items.description: The Kenya refinery is part of Dangote's ambitious bid to expand and help industralise Africa by 2030.

items.title: 'He will never walk free': Indian judge's letter promises child sex abuse survivor
items.description: In the emotional letter, the judge describes the survivor as "the bravest little girl this court has ever seen".

items.title: Singapore launches matchmaking service for government workers
items.description: The launch of FirstDate comes as the ageing nation wrestles with a record-low fertility rate.

items.title: 'Backpack' declared Alaska's Fat Bear Week winner
items.description: "Backpack" defeated a bear known only as "910" in the final round of the annual competition.

items.title: More than 400 detained as France student protests escalate
items.description: Students have been protesting conditions and resources in high schools since last week.

items.title: Restaurant named after Xi Jinping attacked by Chinese nationals in South Korea
items.description: The owner said he chose the name because he wanted to run the "best Chinese restaurant" in South Korea.

items.title: Somali pirates killed oil tanker crew before rescue, official tells BBC
items.description: Piracy off the Somali coast has increased in recent years after dropping when international naval operations began in 2011.

items.title: Crackdown on South Africa's unsafe streets ordered by president to keep women safe
items.description: The murders of 12 women near Johannesburg has caused a outcry about the scale of violence against women.

items.title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit
items.description: The meeting at the White House came as some tech bosses and experts have called for tighter rules around AI.

items.title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail
items.description: The US journalist says he realised he was a "a pawn in a greater game" when he was not interrogated or tortured by FSB agents.

items.title: Ukraine's prized steel industry left in ruins by Russian missile campaign
items.description: Ukraine's remaining steelworks, a vital part of its economy, have all but ground to a halt because of relentless attacks.
